# EDA notes (auto-generated by src/eda.py)

Data: 3,000,888 rows, 2013-01-01 -> 2017-08-15. Every number below was computed from the data, not typed by hand.

1. Average daily sales (all stores added up) per full year: 2013: 385,767, 2014: 575,479, 2015: 661,759, 2016: 790,834  (+105% from 2013 to 2016): a clear trend, so old and new years should not be treated as equal.
2. Weekends sell +39% compared with Monday-Friday; the best day is Sun and the weakest is Thu.
3. Paydays (15th and last day of the month) sell +1% versus other days of the same month: no clear payday effect in this data.
4. 33 product families; the top 3 (GROCERY I, BEVERAGES, PRODUCE) make 64% of all units, so errors on them matter most.
5. 54 stores; the 10 biggest sell 40% of all units. Store type A has the highest average sales per row and type C the lowest.
6. Promotion information starts on 2014-04-01 (before that onpromotion is always 0). Rows with a promotion sell on average 9.6 times the sales of rows without one (not proof of cause: bigger products are promoted more often).
7. Compared with a normal day of the same month, national holidays +15%, event days -1%, work days +19% (first look only: weekday effects are not removed).
8. Jan 1 is -99% versus a normal day (stores are closed). Dec 25 has NO rows at all in any year.
9. In the 14 days after the 2016-04-16 earthquake, average daily sales were +16% compared with the 14 days before.
10. 31% of all rows have zero sales, and 54 of 1782 store x family series never sold anything up to 2017-06-30 (see the qc_ flags). Family with the most zero days: BOOKS (97%).
